subject: wedding DJs
one_liner: A social network for wedding DJs. Finally, 600 people who understand why you are still talking about table seven.
brand_voice_notes: Treat professional grudges as valuable network activity. Familiar social-network language: friends, feed, groups, memories, suggested connections. Specific wedding-DJ working details, delivered with the calm of a quarterly engagement report. No winks, enthusiasm, em dashes or claims of real service. The AI mistakes disagreement for professional development.

hero.h1: You cleared the dance floor. Tell your entire network.
hero.sub: Afterset connects wedding DJs through mutual vendors, public song disputes and AI-resurfaced grievances. Your next booking is three friend requests away from your last complaint.

features.title: People you may have invoiced
features.blurb: Our AI connects you to photographers, rival DJs and the aunt who asked for the microphone. Shared access to a loading bay counts as a mutual friend.

features.title: Memories with unresolved comments
features.blurb: Every anniversary, we resurface the reception where the power failed during the first dance. Tag the venue again. The algorithm considers this relationship maintenance.

features.title: Private groups. Public conclusions.
features.blurb: Ask 1,800 DJs whether a guest request was reasonable. Afterset ranks the longest arguments first and sends the bride a suggested group invitation.

demo_screen_concept: An Afterset social feed for wedding DJ Leon Briggs. A left navigation filters All posts, Request Tribunal and Venue Watch; a search field filters author, post and group text. The central feed contains a text composer, a guest-request poll with two vote buttons, a venue complaint and an AI-resurfaced first-dance memory. Each post has a reversible applause button and an expandable comment thread with a working comment form. The right rail offers suggested vendor connections that can be connected and removed, plus a disputed-request group invitation. Posting, voting, commenting, filtering and connecting work entirely in browser memory. A visible Reset demo button restores seed data.

design_direction.style: Vibrant block-based record-sleeve modernism. Lilac ground, cobalt type, acid-yellow counters and a single oversized vinyl circle behind the wide DJ photograph. The social feed supplies the layout vernacular; no wedding stationery, scripts or gold foil.
design_direction.archetype: Community/Forum Landing from the bundled library: community value hero, feed preview, member stories, membership pricing. HTML/CSS/vanilla JS per pipeline.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 200ms button and feed-filter feedback. Applause count changes on click. No continuous decoration. Reduced-motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Asymmetric split: large left-aligned Syne headline on lilac, wide framed photograph on the right with a circle of cobalt vinyl behind it and a static social post caption beneath. Primary demo button is cobalt. A lime membership strip anchors the hero. Features are open horizontal text columns, testimonials are a joined member strip, pricing uses a divided subscription ledger. Mobile stacks every section in reading order.
design_direction.design_review: The bundled generator selected vibrant block-based community design, retained here. Its wedding-script pairing repeated the subject stereotype and recent entry; replaced with library Fashion Forward (Syne/Manrope) and custom lilac/cobalt palette. The full style/palette/fonts tuple differs from every one of the last seven entries.

images.rationale: One photographic hero earns its place as the empty-ballroom counterpoint to a busy professional network. Text-based social-feed posts need no demo subject photographs; member avatars reuse the three testimonial portraits. Three remaining slots allocated to deadpan corporate DJ headshots. All four passed vision review on first attempt: correct single subject, coordinated palette, no readable text artifacts, credible photographic detail.

items.prompt: Editorial flash photograph for a vibrant record-sleeve campaign: one male wedding DJ in his late forties, plain dark suit and loose lilac tie, plain over-ear headphones around neck, standing alone behind a modest unbranded DJ mixing booth in an empty hotel ballroom after a reception. Only one person. Folded pale lilac napkins and empty dance floor; deadpan, professionally composed, directly looking at camera. Medium-wide horizontal composition, man on right third, ordinary real hotel interior, lilac #EFECF8 walls with cobalt #4936CF stage light, subtle acid yellow #EDFF82 accent, analog flash texture, realistic imperfect skin and room details. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.
items.judge_verdict: Pass: subject, palette, photographic detail and no-text checks.
